title: 2016 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement: A contest has six problems worth seven points each. On any given problem, a contestant can score either 0,1 , or 7 points. How many possible total scores can a contestant achieve over all six problems?

solutions.text:
Answer: 28
For \(0 \leq k \leq 6\), to obtain a score that is \(k(\bmod 6)\) exactly \(k\) problems must get a score of 1 . The remaining \(6-k\) problems can generate any multiple of 7 from 0 to \(7(6-k)\), of which there are \(7-k\). So the total number of possible scores is \(\sum_{k=0}^{6}(7-k)=28\).
